text:
alex: Heads-up — want to propose a pattern for ephemeral RBAC grants for our SAST/DAST scanners so they can decrypt test artifacts via KMS briefly, but still produce tamper-evident audit logs. Thinking: time-limited service-role, short-lived token, and append-only evidence bundle. Thoughts?

maya: +1 on ephemeral roles. main question: how do we ensure the evidence bundle itself is auditable and can't be swapped after the scan?

devon: we should HMAC the bundle and store the signature in KMS-wrapped metadata or in our audit log backend. even a small manifest.json with sha256 sums helps.

samir: agree. KMS's envelope encryption + storing the signing key in KMS is fine. but need to avoid long-lived keys in build runners. prefer using short-lived KMS grants via an agent.

alex: prototype idea: runner requests ephemeral grant from auth-service -> auth-service calls KMS:GenerateDataKey (with GrantTokens?) -> runner uses data key to decrypt artifact -> runner uploads results+manifest -> audit-service records signature+grant-id.

security-bot: Reminder: policy SEC-LOG-3 requires retention of scan evidence for 90 days and immutable audit entries for 365 days. Ensure audit-service is WORM-like. :lock:

maya: operational concern: what happens if decryption fails mid-scan? we need to capture partial evidence and log grant usage with failure reason. don’t want undetected silent failures.

devon: add a small retry wrapper in the GH Action and emit a structured log line on failure. Example snippet: ```yaml
- name: Decrypt artifact
  run: |
    set -e
    ./decrypt --grant-token \"$GRANT_TOKEN\" artifact.enc || (
      echo \"scan_decrypt_failure: $RETRY_COUNT\" >&2
      echo \"{\"event\":\"decrypt_failure\",\"artifact\":\"$ART\",\"reason\":\"$?\"}\" >> /tmp/scan_events.json
      exit 1
    )
```

samir: also, bind grants to a specific scan run id and ephemeral role so grant IDs in KMS map back to a single audit entry. that helps during incident triage.

alex: question for ops: should we allow the scanner to call KMS directly, or route through our auth-service proxy that enforces RBAC and attaches metadata?

maya: proxy is safer. it can inject run metadata and create the audit row in the same TX as issuing the grant. plus easier to rotate/ban if we detect abuse.

devon: one downside: proxy adds latency for large-scale parallel scans. but scans are batch jobs, so small added latency OK.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline #4821: sast-scan job failed (decrypt error) — retry queued by devex.

alex: thanks — that failure is exactly why I want stronger visibility into grants. we had a case last week where two PRs saw intermittent decrypt errors and it was just logged in runner logs, not central audit.

samir: proposed runbook steps: 1) issue ephemeral grant via proxy with run_id and scanner_id 2) store grant_id + run_id in audit-service 3) scanner runs and uploads bundle + manifest + signature 4) audit-service validates signature and marks run complete 5) on failure, mark run failed and include grant failure reason + runner logs in evidence.

maya: + add an automatic oncall alert if >3 decrypt failures for same scanner within 10m. helps catch infra regressions.

devon: also include a checksum verification step before calling the parser — prevents feeding malformed test artifacts into scanner.

alex: any objections to using KMS GenerateDataKey with a restrict_policy that includes the run_id and a short TTL (e.g., 15m)?

samir: fine. but verify we can audit the policy restrictions later. KMS audit entries need to include the grant context. ensure CloudAudit logs have the grant-id in the entry.

security-bot: Note: create ticket to update SA-7 (Key management controls) if we change grant flows. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1234

alex: action items: @maya to draft proxy API (endpoints + minimal required metadata), @devon to add GH Action snippet and manifest format, @samir to prototype KMS grant flow + proof-of-concept that stores grant-id in audit-service. I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow 10:30 PT.

maya: will do. starting with API shape: POST /v1/scan-grants {run_id, scanner_id, ttl_seconds, allowed_artifact_digest} -> returns {grant_token, grant_id, expiry}.

devon: manifest format suggestion: {\"run_id\":\"...\",\"files\":[{\"path\":\"...\",\"sha256\":\"...\"}],\"signature\":\"...\",\"signer\":\"scanner@redwood\"}  — keep compact.

samir: fyi: when prototyping, set KMS logging level to DEBUG so we can confirm grant_id shows up in audit logs, then flip to INFO.

alex: thanks all. if nobody objects, I'll make the ticket and mark this as RFC for next-week change window. :white_check_mark:

maya: no objections. 

devon: ack.

security-bot: Policy check: proposed design meets SEC-LOG-3 & SA-7 baseline pending ticket review.

alex: closing thread — will post RFC link after I create the ticket.
